doc.title: Jerry Jerome interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Play the melody, and moving into conducting and jingles
summary: He moved into NBC conducting, arranging and a jingle company for 25 years, then returned to playing after retiring to Sarasota.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: There’s a company in Chicago that puts out bumper stickers that says “play the melody.”
Yeah, because I don’t know they’re into the old —

Dave Capp had a big sign, with an Indian like this, praying to heaven. And the sign says “play the melody.” In the Decca studios. So that was the money part of playing it. So I hung in with this for a long time, and went into conducting at NBC and studying arranging and composing, and formed my own company to write jingles for 25 years. I didn’t do much playing horn at that time except when we’d have a session and the guys would come in, I’d do that. And then I came down here to Sarasota to retire, and picked up the horn again, and I’ve been playing concerts, and going back to blowing the horn again.
